questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the two main uses of fāngmiàn?
How does qíngxing relate to qíngkuàng?
What happens to the tone when a one-syllable adjectival verb is doubled in Běijīng speech?
Name the four meanings of mànmanr.
Write the Chinese for "There are two aspects to this question."
Write the Chinese for "Sit down and I'll give you the whole story."

answers.answer_text: Nǐ zuòxia, wǒ mànmanr gēn ni jiǎng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which of qíngkuàng and qíngxing is more common in present-day Běijīng speech?

answers.answer_text: Qíngkuàng — at least among the younger generation.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give two other examples of doubled adjectival verbs used as adverbs.
Write the Chinese for "Let's take our time walking. We'll make it."

articles.text:
8. A: Nǐ qùde nèige dìfang,          What was the political and economic
      zhèngzhì, jīngjì fāngmiànde     situation like where you went?
      qíngxing zěnmeyàng?
   B: Jǐjù huà shuōbuqīngchu, yǒu    I can't explain it clearly in just a
      shíjiān wǒ zài gēn ni           few sentences; when I have time
      mànmanr shuō ba.                I'll tell you all about it.

Notes on No. 8

fāngmiàn: "aspect; area; respect; side." This noun is used WITHOUT a counter. It is a useful, sometimes overused word. When translating, it is sometimes better just to leave fāngmiàn out of the English.

Fāngmiàn has two main uses:

(1) "aspect, respect, area, field"

Zhèige wèntí yǒu liǎngfāngmiàn.  There are two aspects to this question.
Wǒmen zài zhèifāngmiàn zuòde     We haven't done enough in this area.
hái bù gòu.
Wǒ méi shìde shíhou xǐhuan       When I don't have anything to do I
kànkan wénxué fāngmiànde shū.    like to read books on literature.

(2) "party, side," referring to a group of people

Guānyú zhèige wèntí, liǎng       The two sides have somewhat different
fāngmiànde kànfǎ yǒu diǎn        views on this question.
bù tóng.

qíngxing: In most cases interchangeable with qíngkuàng. In present-day Běijīng speech, at least among the younger generation, qíngkuàng is the more common of these two words.

shuōbuqīngchu: "can't say/explain clearly." Shuōqīngchu is a compound verb of result.

Wǒ shuōbuqīngchu wèishénme tā    I can't really explain why he got
shēngqì.                         angry.
Tā shuōqīngchule tāde mùdì.      He explained his goal clearly.

mànmanr: Also mànmān. Many adjectival verbs can be DOUBLED to make an adverb, which is used between the subject and the verb. In Běijīng speech, when you double certain one-syllable adjectival verbs, the second one becomes FIRST TONE (no matter what its original tone) and -r is added. Other examples are kuàikuāirde, "quickly," and hǎohāorde, "well, properly."

Mànman(de) or mànmanr(de) has these meanings:

(1) "slowly"
Tā mànmanrde zǒu huí jiā qu le.  He slowly walked home.

(2) "gradually, bit by bit, by and by"
Mànmanrde, tā jiu dǒng le.       Gradually he began to understand.

(3) "take your time..., don't rush"
Mànmanr zǒu, zánmen láidejí.     Let's take our time walking. We'll
                                 make it.

(4) With verbs meaning "to tell," mànmanr has more of the meaning "in all details."
Nǐ zuòxia, wǒ mànmanr gēn ni     Sit down and I'll give you the whole
jiǎng.                           story.
